title: Advertising to Early Trend Propagators: Evidence from Twitter
eligible_reason: Not a DiD or event-study design. Field tests compare early vs late posters on a Twitter trend using a continuous regressor (days since trend) in an aggregate logit model with day, trend and message fixed effects.
design_notes: Two Twitter promoted-tweet field tests (a charity and a fashion firm). Equation (1): Engagement_ijkt = b1 DaysSinceTrend_ijt + b2 Targeting_j + b3 Message_k + delta_t + e, estimated as an aggregate logit by maximum likelihood on campaign-day data (impressions as trials, engagements as successes). Treatment is a continuous timing variable, not a binary switch at unit-specific dates; units are campaign-days, not stable units tracked over time. The Bertrand-Duflo-Mullainathan citation only justifies clustering SEs at the campaign level.
screener_notes: Not eligible: no DiD design, continuous treatment, nonlinear model. Data from the authors' field tests with a charity and a fashion firm; no data availability statement and no replication package listed. Screened from article text only.
